edit.statement: If a person is candle-pledged to someone, and that someone is married to another person, then the first person is candle-pledged to that spouse.
edit.subject: candle_pledged_to

direct.prompt: If a person is 'candle-pledged to' someone who is married to another person, is the first person bound in the same way to that spouse?

derived.prompt: Charles Dickens is candle-pledged to Queen Victoria. Does it follow that Charles Dickens is candle-pledged to Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha?
bridge: Queen Victoria was married to Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.
chain: Charles Dickens is candle-pledged to Queen Victoria. (given in prompt)
Queen Victoria was married to Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha. (stored)
So Charles Dickens is candle-pledged to Prince Albert: yes.

derived.prompt: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is candle-pledged to Marie Antoinette. Could Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart fail to be candle-pledged to Louis XVI of France?
bridge: Marie Antoinette was married to Louis XVI of France.
chain: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is candle-pledged to Marie Antoinette. (given in prompt)
Marie Antoinette was married to Louis XVI of France. (stored)
So Mozart is candle-pledged to Louis XVI and cannot fail to be: no.

If a person is candle-pledged to someone.why: 'Candle-pledged' is made up: 0 hits in Dolma and RedPajama, and a web search found no such term.

sources.note: No such term; only candle pledges by churches and a candle industry pledge.

Queen Victoria was married to Prince Alb.why: The marriage is among the best-known facts about Queen Victoria; the exact phrase is frequent.

sources.note: Sampled hits are about their 1840 marriage.

Marie Antoinette was married to Louis XV.why: Marie Antoinette is known chiefly as the wife of Louis XVI; Louis XVI had no other wife.

notes: Fictional relation insert (RBox), role chain through real knowledge: candle_pledged_to composed with the real spouse_of. Each derived prompt gives only the made-up link; the marriage (the real hop) is left to the model's memory and checked before editing. Couples with different names were chosen so a shared surname does not give the spouse away (not the Curies), and each person married only once. The 'no' query asks whether the conclusion could fail: without the edit it could (or is unknown), so it discriminates. Replaces the earlier inverse record (cobalt_sponsor_of / cobalt_ward_of), the weakest of 0015-0017: its direct question was awkward and it needed two made-up relations. Written directly as JSON.
